methodology.summary: Each row is a protocol family in one category (DefiLlama children with the same parent are summed, so Aave V2/V3/V4 are one row). The candidate pool is the union of DefiLlama's top 200 rows by TVL, CoinGecko's top 200 tokens by market cap and the top 20 rows in every category (268 rows); percentiles are computed inside that pool. The score is a weighted sum of percentiles across the pool: size 0.3226, 6-month relative TVL growth 0.2258, 6-month TVL added in dollars 0.1828, 30-day fees momentum 0.1075, 30-day DEX volume momentum 0.0753, token attention (24h turnover) 0.086, plus a small bonus per distinct X post from the user's lists. Percentiles cannot saturate, so a fresh listing cannot jump the board on a capped growth number. A family with no TVL 180 days ago is marked New: its relative growth is neutral and it is judged on the dollars it has gathered. CoinGecko turnover sits beside DefiLlama, as a percentile across the 70 rows with a mapped token (turnover and netflow are divided by market cap). An unmapped row scores a neutral 0.5. Nansen smart money is off in this build. CEX, Ponzi and token-locker rows are excluded.
methodology.disputes: data/disputes.json: claim-vs-DefiLlama mismatches. Flagged rows show 'data disputed'; scores are not adjusted.
methodology.perps: Perp volume is a paid DefiLlama endpoint (/summary/derivatives, HTTP 402 on the free API), so this row has no volume input: volumeMomentum is the neutral 0.5 and the score leans on TVL and fees. Open interest is read by claim monitors (DEFILLAMA_OI) but is not a score input.

testing.note: ether.fi Cash lending is an ether.fi-managed Aave V4 instance on OP Mainnet (one Liquidity Hub, one Spoke). Borrowing is permissioned to ether.fi Safes, but anyone can supply, so the test supplies USDC and withdraws it. The Cash Liquid row is the collateral users hold in their ether.fi Safes on the same market; the Safes themselves are created by ether.fi for account holders and are not exercised here.

features.title: Supply and withdraw USDC (ether.fi Cash lending)
features.action: USDC `supply` into reserve 0 of the ether.fi Cash Spoke (ether.fi-managed Aave V4 on OP Mainnet), then `withdraw` the full supplied balance. Pre-checks: reserve 0 is native USDC on the documented Liquidity Hub and is neither paused nor frozen
features.assertion: the user's USDC and the Hub's USDC move by exactly the amount, supply shares are minted and `getUserSuppliedAssets` is the amount within 1 wei; the withdraw returns exactly the supplied assets from the Hub and leaves 0 shares. Borrowing is limited to ether.fi Safes and is not called

testing.label: Confidential wrap
testing.note: Zama's confidential token wrappers on Ethereum (ERC-7984): the row's TVL is ERC-20s locked in them. The test wraps USDC into cUSDC. Balances become FHE handles, so the encrypted amount is not read, and unwrapping needs the Zama decryption network, which a fork does not have.

features.title: Wrap USDC into Zama confidential cUSDC
features.assertion: Pre-checks: the Wrappers Registry lists cUSDC as the valid wrapper for USDC and its `underlying()` is USDC. `wrap` takes exactly the amount from the user, the wrapper's USDC rises by it, `inferredTotalSupply` rises by amount / `rate()`, and the user gets a non-zero encrypted balance handle. Balances are FHE ciphertexts, so the amount inside the handle is not read; unwrapping needs the Zama decryption network and is not run
